newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.93/0.88 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 0.88/0.83 percent. One-year was unchanged from Wednesday's yield of 1.43/1.38 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.25/99.30 against Wednesday's close of S$99.18/99.23, September 2001 at S$97.38/97.43 versus S$97.39/97.44 and June 2003 at S$95.38/95.43 from S$95.43/95.48.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent against Wednesday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
